biggest_gap.title: The audit log takes minutes to print or export, and that alone stops the isolation gate from finishing
biggest_gap.detail: Printing or exporting the audit log through the reports framework is about 25 times slower than any other list. On the demo, at the same machine load, the audit log as PDF took 360 s in English and 399 s in Arabic (134 MB), and as XLSX 262 s. The 100,000-row users and exchange-rate lists print as Arabic PDF in 14 to 16 s. Inside the gate suite, the test tenant's audit log grows with every write, and G1HttpIsolationTests asks for every print shape (pdf/xlsx, en/ar, latn/arab digits, every groupBy, inline/attachment) again on every read round. Those requests averaged 11.3 s and reached 84.8 s, and they slow whatever runs beside them. Some request then passes the 100 s client timeout and the attack aborts. This happened in all 4 runs today, so ./erp verify --clean-clone fails and the gate never gets to judge the product. The integrator's alone run passed only on a quiet machine. For a UAE trading company the same weakness shows up directly: an auditor or accountant who presses Print or export on a filtered trail waits minutes. Even when it finishes, the export cuts each change's 'Old and new values' to 200 characters, so it is not a complete audit record.
biggest_gap.evidence: demo-print-timings.txt (critic's demo at http://localhost:20750, admin@alnoor.example): /api/reports/lists/audit.log?format=pdf&language=en 360.5 s, 33.8 MB; ...&language=ar&numerals=arab&groupBy=action 398.8 s, 133.9 MB; ?format=xlsx 262.0 s; /api/reports/lists/identity.users?format=pdf&language=ar 15.6 s; /api/reports/lists/currency.rates?format=pdf&language=ar 13.9 s. plants/g1http-slow-requests.log (unplanted G1HttpIsolationTests with a timing hook): /api/reports/lists/audit.log in 134 of 146 requests over 5 s, average 11.3 s, maximum 84.8 s; the final abort was GET /api/numbering/sequences after 104.8 s. Failures: verify-critic-p07-audit-r2-run1.log (G1HttpIsolationTests at 1 h 7 m, G1ListVolumeTests at 24 m 52 s) and verify-critic-p07-audit-r2-run2.log (G1HttpIsolationTests at 1 h 50 m, ParameterAttackAsync line 672), each 'The client aborted the request'. To reproduce: ./erp up, sign in as admin@alnoor.example, then time GET /api/reports/lists/audit.log?format=pdf. The 200-character cut is AuditTexts.SummaryLength = 200; see the CSV export ending with 'Sort: -o…'.

gate_gaps.gate: AuditTrailTests (module tests) and G2PermissionTests: nothing checks that GET /api/audit/log/{id} applies the per-kind and per-company read filter (AuditReader.VisibleAsync)
gate_gaps.planted: In AuditEndpoints.Change, replaced the VisibleAsync-filtered query with reader.Db.AuditEntries.AsNoTracking() (plants/P1-log-change-skips-kind-filter.diff). A user whose role holds only identity.roles.read and audit.log.read then reads a user's change, with every stored old and new value, by its id.
gate_gaps.evidence: With P1 planted, all 11 AuditTrailTests passed and every G2PermissionTests test passed except the one caught by the P2 plant (plant-critic-p07-r2-run1.log). The critic's added check (plant-P1-control-test.diff: the 'Roles auditor' asks GET /api/audit/log/<a change of identity.users>) got 200 under the plant and 404 on the real product. So the real product is clean and the gate is blind.

other_findings: Run 1 web stage: 2 tests in src/modules/shell/clientIsolation.test.tsx failed at load 117. One was the 'one tab, tenant B then tenant A' test timing out at 30 s; the second test failed after it ('Cannot read properties of null'). Run alone at load ~2, each takes 19.2 s against its 30 s limit. Both passed in run 2. This is load-sensitive.

Run 1: G1ListVolumeTests (demo volume) failed on a client timeout. In a diagnostic run at load ~15 it passed (21 m 39 s), and its slowest queries were all audit-log searches with one or two letters, up to 7.6 s (e.g. /api/audit/log?take=50&search=k&groupBy=action). It passed in run 2.

Export cuts values short: 'Old and new values' in the audit log CSV/XLSX/PDF is one line capped at 200 characters (AuditTexts.SummaryLength). Full old and new values come only one change at a time from GET /api/audit/log/{id}. The export row limit is 200,000, while the demo log holds 400,000+ rows.
CSV export: 'Changed by' is empty for seed and system rows (the API says 'Demo data'), and 'Fields' exports a count ('8') instead of the field names.

The log list's 'Old and new values' column shows raw ISO timestamps (e.g. 'Expires: 2026-11-02T19:27:35.9617…', and in Arabic 'ينتهي في: القيمة 2026-11-02T19:27:59…'). The change panel formats the same values as local dates. Role permissions show as raw keys (identity.roles.read).

Tamper evidence: erp_app holds INSERT on audit.entries, and audit.capture() is not SECURITY DEFINER. So the application role can insert made-up audit rows in its own tenant, with any actor_id and a back-dated occurred_at; the critic did this as erp_app and the insert succeeded (rolled back). UPDATE and DELETE are refused as required.

A record's history on its form needs audit.log.read. The demo's 'Company manager' role (reads companies, branches and users) therefore sees no history on any form. AuditPermissions.LogRead's own doc comment says 'A record's own history on its form needs only the record's read permission', which the History endpoint and the web extension (permission: audit.log.read) contradict.
Sign-in sessions fill the log: every sign-in writes an identity.sessions audit row (IP, browser, hidden key), so person-made business changes are hard to see without a filter.

Scope otherwise present and working in a real Chromium, by keyboard, in English and Arabic RTL: the latest-change line under the record heading, the History panel (Alt+Y, Escape closes), G then L to the audit log (400,358 changes, total shown), search by record name, column filters (who, change, record type, record, fields, when), a change panel linking to its record, and print/export. Custom fields are recorded field by field in the trigger (custom_fields.<key>); no custom-field module is integrated yet to try it end to end.

Stage wall times were dotnet 7,428 s, web 4,699 s and e2e 8,278 s, at load 2 to 47 from other critics' verifies. During run 1 the critic's own demo stack was also up, with load up to 117.
